title: Add filters to a tiny template engine
prompt: The template engine in the `tmpl` package (`tmpl.render(template, context)`) supports `{{ name }}` and dotted lookups like `{{ user.name }}`; a missing variable renders as an empty string. Add filters with this syntax: `{{ expr|filter }}`, chained left to right as in `{{ name|default:"anon"|upper }}`, with optional whitespace around the expression, each `|`, and inside the braces (`{{ name | upper }}`). Filters: `upper` and `lower` convert the value to str and change its case (a missing value stays ""); `default:"text"` replaces the value with the given text when the variable is missing, None, or the empty string (the argument is always a double-quoted string, may contain spaces and colons, but no double quotes or `|`). A value that is not missing is converted with str(). An unknown filter name raises `tmpl.errors.TemplateError` with the message `unknown filter: <name>`. Text outside `{{ }}` must be left untouched, and templates without filters must render exactly as before. Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.
